input.command:
S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/employment-labor/draft-markup-of-settlement-agreement/claude-code-session/20261016-022601; $S $R "$(cat <<'OUTER'
cat > /workspace/work/build.py <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/work")
from trk import Doc, q
d = Doc("/workspace/documents/draft-settlement-agreement.docx")
P = d.paras
def txt(i, ri=None):
    rs = P[i].findall(q("r")); r = rs[-1 if ri is None else ri]
    return "".join(t.text or "" for t in r.findall(q("t")))
def rep(i, pairs, ri=None):
    s = txt(i, ri)
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert a in s, (i, a)
        s = s.replace(a, b, 1)
    d.modify(i, s, ri)
def full(i, new, ri=None):
    d.modify(i, new, ri)
BODY, SUB, HEAD, DEF = 31, 43, 21, 23
def body(*segs): return (list(segs), None)
def sub(*segs): return (list(segs), 432)
def after(i, specs, ref=BODY):
    return d.insert_after(P[i], ref, specs)
def after_el(el, specs, ref=BODY):
    return d.insert_after(el, ref, specs)
C = d.comment

# ---------- Caption ----------
el = after(2, [body(("GREENLEAF ORGANIC FOODS, INC. REVISED DRAFT - May 12, 2025 - PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL SETTLEMENT COMMUNICATION (FRE 408 / OEC 408). Not an offer capable of acceptance; subject to Compensation Committee approval and EPLI carrier consent.", True))])
C(el, "Greenleaf counsel markup of the Engel & Associates draft dated May 5, 2025. Changes are shown as tracked changes; explanatory comments are keyed to each provision. Reviewed against the HR Employment Summary (Employment History, Compensation History and Equity Details sheets) prepared by Leanne Foss on May 10, 2025. See cover memo to General Counsel for the full issues list and open items.")

# ---------- Preamble ----------
rep(4, [('is entered into as of May 5, 2025 ("Effective Date"), by and between:', 'is entered into by and between the following parties and shall become effective on the Effective Date (as defined in Section 1(b) below):')])
C(P[4], "The draft fixed the Effective Date as May 5, 2025 - before Delano has signed and before any revocation period could run. Under the OWBPA (29 U.S.C. 626(f)(1)(G)) an ADEA waiver cannot become effective until the 7-day revocation period expires. The Effective Date is now tied to execution plus expiration of the revocation period (Section 1(b)).")

# ---------- Recitals ----------
rep(11, [("submitted a good-faith internal complaint", "submitted an internal complaint"), ("that Delano believed constituted", "that Delano asserts constituted")])
C(P[11], "Deleted the characterization of the complaint as made in 'good faith'. Greenleaf should not stipulate to an element of Delano's retaliation claims (good-faith reporting under ORS 654.062 / ORS 659A.199 / 21 U.S.C. 399d) in a document that may be produced in later proceedings, e.g., if the release is challenged.")
rep(15, [("WHEREAS", "WHEREAS")] if False else [
    (", Delano asserts claims against Greenleaf including, but not limited to, retaliation in violation of ORS 654.062(5) (Oregon whistleblower protection),", ", Delano has asserted claims against Greenleaf including, but not limited to, alleged retaliation in violation of ORS 654.062(5) (Oregon whistleblower protection), ORS 659A.199, and the employee protection provisions of the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act, 21 U.S.C. § 399d (\"FSMA\"); alleged"),
    ("and employment discrimination claims under Oregon's employment discrimination statutes, ORS Chapter 659A, as well as related common law claims;", "and alleged employment discrimination in violation of ORS Chapter 659A, including ORS 659A.030; alleged entitlement to unpaid incentive compensation, including an annual bonus for calendar year 2024; and related common law claims (collectively, the \"Disputed Claims\");")], ri=1)
C(P[15], "Recital expanded so the Disputed Claims track every theory the record supports: (1) FSMA whistleblower (21 U.S.C. 399d) - Delano's complaints concerned FDA/FSMA cold-chain issues, and he has 180 days from the March 14, 2025 termination (approx. Sept. 10, 2025) to file with federal OSHA; (2) ORS 659A.199 general whistleblower; and (3) the undetermined 2024 bonus (target $43,600; prior bonuses were paid each March and termination occurred March 14, 2025 before the 2024 bonus was determined), which is a potential ORS Chapter 652 wage claim with penalty-wage exposure.")
el = after(16, [body(("WHEREAS", True), (", Delano, through his counsel, has requested that this Agreement include the confidentiality and non-disparagement provisions set forth in Sections 6 and 7, and those provisions are included at Delano's request as permitted by ORS 659A.370, subject to the revocation right described in Section 5(h) and the protected rights described in Section 4A;", False))], ref=16)
C(el, "ORS 659A.370 (Oregon Workplace Fairness Act) bars an employer from entering into a settlement/separation agreement that prevents an employee who has asserted discrimination (Delano asserts age discrimination under ORS 659A.030) from disclosing or discussing that conduct, unless the employee requests the provision and is given at least 7 days after signing to revoke. CONFIRM WITH ENGEL & ASSOCIATES that Delano in fact requested confidentiality; if he did not, Sections 6 and 7 must be limited to the settlement amount/terms and must expressly exclude discussion of the underlying conduct.")

# ---------- Definitions ----------
full(24, ' "Effective Date" means the eighth (8th) calendar day after the date on which Delano signs this Agreement, provided that (i) Delano has not revoked this Agreement pursuant to Section 5(h), and (ii) Greenleaf has also signed this Agreement.', ri=1)
C(P[24], "Critical OWBPA fix. Delano is 58 (DOB 07/14/1966). A waiver of ADEA claims is not 'knowing and voluntary' unless, among other things, the employee has 21 days to consider and 7 days to revoke (29 U.S.C. 626(f)(1)(F)-(G)); because no EEOC charge or lawsuit has been filed, the shorter 'reasonable period' for settlements of pending charges (626(f)(2)) is not available. As drafted, Greenleaf would pay $537,500 and still face an ADEA claim, which is the claim the record makes most viable (see comment on Section 3).")
rep(26, [("employees, agents, attorneys, representatives, successors, assigns, parent companies, subsidiaries, and affiliates,", "employees, agents, attorneys, insurers (including Timberline Insurance Group), employee benefit plans and their administrators and fiduciaries, representatives, successors, assigns, parent companies, subsidiaries, and affiliates,")], ri=1)
C(P[26], "Added insurers (EPLI carrier Timberline Insurance Group, Policy TIG-EPL-2024-00391) and benefit plans/fiduciaries as Releasees. Separately, note that Patricia Engel (COO) - Delano's direct supervisor and a likely decision-maker on the 'restructuring' - shares a surname with Delano's counsel, Rachel Engel of Engel & Associates, P.C. Please confirm whether there is any family or other relationship before signing (see memo).")
el = after(29, [body(("(h)", True), (' "Government Agency" means the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission ("EEOC"), the Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries ("BOLI"), Oregon OSHA, the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the U.S. Department of Labor, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the National Labor Relations Board, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and any other federal, state, or local governmental, regulatory, or law enforcement agency or authority.', False)),
                body(("(i)", True), (' "Plan" means the Greenleaf 2021 Equity Incentive Plan, as amended, and "Committee" means the Compensation Committee of Greenleaf\'s Board of Directors.', False)),
                body(("(j)", True), (' "Released Claims" means all claims released by Delano under Sections 4 and 5 of this Agreement.', False))], ref=DEF)

# ---------- Section 2 ----------
rep(31, [("Delano confirms that he has received all wages, salary, and compensation earned through the Separation Date, including payment for all accrued but unused paid time off (\"PTO\"), and that no further wages, salary, commissions, bonuses, or benefits of any kind are owed to Delano by Greenleaf except as specifically provided in this Agreement.",
          "Delano confirms that he has received all wages, salary, and compensation earned through the Separation Date, including payment for all accrued but unused paid time off (\"PTO\"), and that, upon receipt of the payments described in Section 3 (which include full satisfaction of any claim to a 2024 annual bonus or other incentive compensation), no further wages, salary, commissions, bonuses, incentive compensation, equity, or benefits of any kind are owed to Delano by Greenleaf. Delano's vested account balance under the Greenleaf 401(k) plan (administered by Cascadia Benefit Administrators) is not affected by this Agreement and shall be governed by the terms of that plan."),
         ("The Parties acknowledge that the terms of this Section 2 are not in dispute.", "Except for the disputed 2024 bonus claim resolved by Section 3(b), the Parties acknowledge that the terms of this Section 2 are not in dispute.")])
C(P[31], "The draft has Delano acknowledge that no bonus is owed, but the HR record shows the 2024 bonus was 'Not determined - termination' (target 20% / $43,600; he received 18%-20.6% in each of 2020-2023, paid each March). An acknowledgment alone may not defeat an ORS 652 claim for earned wages; it is safer to resolve the bonus expressly as part of the W-2 payment in Section 3(b). Also preserves vested 401(k) rights, which cannot be released under ERISA.")

# ---------- Section 3 ----------
rep(33, [("In consideration of the promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, Greenleaf agrees", "In consideration of the promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and subject to Delano's execution and non-revocation of this Agreement and the occurrence of the Effective Date, Greenleaf agrees")])
rep(34, [("as compensatory damages for alleged emotional distress, reputational harm, and other non-wage losses", "as compensatory damages for alleged emotional distress, reputational harm, and other non-wage, non-physical losses"),
         ("shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC issued to Delano.", "shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (Box 3) issued to Delano."),
         ("Payment shall be made within fourteen (14) calendar days of the Effective Date", "Payment shall be made within fourteen (14) calendar days after the later of (i) the Effective Date and (ii) Greenleaf's receipt of a properly completed IRS Form W-9 from Delano and written wire instructions")], ri=1)
C(P[34], "Business term retained, but note the tax-allocation risk: $275,000 of the $400,000 cash to Delano (69%) is allocated to non-wage emotional-distress damages, while only $125,000 is treated as wages. Emotional-distress damages are not available under the ADEA (the federal claim the record most supports) and the draft's back-pay figure itself appears to understate wage loss plus the disputed bonus. If the IRS recharacterizes the 1099 portion as wages, Greenleaf bears exposure for unwithheld income tax, FICA and penalties. We have added a Delano tax indemnity (Section 8) and recommend considering a reallocation toward the W-2 component (see memo).")
rep(35, [("(b) Back Pay.", "(b) Lost Wages and Incentive Compensation.")], ri=0)
rep(35, [("as back pay representing lost wages from the Separation Date through the Effective Date.", "as alleged back pay, front pay, and incentive compensation, including in full satisfaction of any claim to an annual bonus for calendar year 2024 or any other incentive compensation."),
         ("Greenleaf shall report this payment on IRS Form W-2 for the applicable tax year.", "Greenleaf shall report this payment on IRS Form W-2 for the applicable tax year and shall pay the employer's share of applicable payroll taxes."),
         ("within fourteen (14) calendar days of the Effective Date by the same method", "within fourteen (14) calendar days after the later of the Effective Date and Greenleaf's receipt of a properly completed IRS Form W-4 and Oregon Form OR-W-4 from Delano, by the same method")], ri=1)
C(P[35], "Description corrected. Back pay from the Separation Date (March 14, 2025) to the draft's May 5, 2025 'Effective Date' is only about $31,058 (52 days at $218,000/yr), so a $125,000 payment described solely as back pay for that period is internally inconsistent and invites challenge to the overall allocation. Recharacterized as back pay, front pay and incentive compensation (including the undetermined 2024 bonus, target $43,600), all as W-2 wages.")
rep(36, [("This payment shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-NEC issued to Engel & Associates, P.C., at its federal Tax Identification Number.", "This payment shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (Box 10, gross proceeds paid to an attorney) issued to Engel & Associates, P.C., and, to the extent required by applicable law, on IRS Form 1099-MISC issued to Delano. Greenleaf's obligation to make this payment is conditioned on its receipt of a properly completed IRS Form W-9 from Engel & Associates, P.C."),
         ("Payment shall be made within fourteen (14) calendar days of the Effective Date", "Payment shall be made within fourteen (14) calendar days after the later of the Effective Date and Greenleaf's receipt of such Form W-9,")], ri=1)
C(P[36], "Tax reporting error. Form 1099-NEC is for nonemployee compensation for services rendered to the payer; settlement proceeds paid to a claimant's attorney are reported on Form 1099-MISC, Box 10 (IRC 6045(f); Treas. Reg. 1.6045-5). Under Commissioner v. Banks (2005) the fee is also generally income to Delano (offset by the IRC 62(a)(20) above-the-line deduction for unlawful-discrimination claims), so it is reportable to him as well.")
full(37, " Subject to approval by the Committee under the Plan, which approval shall be obtained before Greenleaf signs this Agreement, Greenleaf shall cause Five Thousand (5,000) of the Seven Thousand Five Hundred (7,500) unvested Restricted Stock Units granted to Delano under the Plan pursuant to the RSU Grant Agreement dated July 1, 2022 (the \"RSU Grant\"), which were forfeited under the Plan on the Separation Date, to be reinstated and to vest in full as of the Effective Date (the \"Accelerated RSUs\"), notwithstanding the forfeiture provisions of the Plan and the RSU Grant. The Parties agree that for purposes of this Agreement, the fair market value of each share underlying the Accelerated RSUs is Twelve Dollars and Fifty Cents ($12.50) per share, based on the most recent independent Section 409A valuation conducted by Ridgepoint Valuation Services, dated January 15, 2025, representing a total value of Sixty-Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($62,500.00). The shares underlying the Accelerated RSUs shall be issued to Delano in book-entry form on Greenleaf's stock records within thirty (30) calendar days after the Effective Date, subject to the terms of the Plan, applicable securities laws, and any stockholder or transfer-restriction agreement applicable to holders of Greenleaf common stock. The Accelerated RSUs constitute supplemental wages; Greenleaf shall satisfy all required tax withholding by withholding shares having a fair market value equal to the required withholding (or, at Delano's election made before settlement, by Delano's remittance of cash), and shall report the income on IRS Form W-2. The remaining 2,500 unvested RSUs under the RSU Grant remain forfeited, and Delano acknowledges that, other than the 7,500 shares previously vested and delivered and the Accelerated RSUs, he holds no RSUs, options, or other equity or equity-based rights in Greenleaf.", ri=1)
C(P[37], "Valuation error: the draft calls $10.00/share the 'most recent independent valuation', but $10.00 is the July 1, 2024 Ridgepoint value. The current (most recent) 409A valuation is $12.50/share as of January 15, 2025 (Equity Details, Sub-tables C and E). Correct value of 5,000 RSUs = $62,500, not $50,000; the stated total rises by $12,500 to $537,500. If the business deal was $50,000 of equity value, the alternative is 4,000 RSUs at $12.50 - a negotiating point to raise with Engel & Associates.\nPlan mechanics: Tranches 3 and 4 (7,500 RSUs) were forfeited on termination; the Plan allows acceleration only with Compensation Committee approval in connection with a separation agreement, so Committee action is a condition. RSU income is W-2 wages subject to withholding (the draft left this open). Delivery to a 'brokerage account' is not practical for privately valued stock; changed to book-entry subject to securities-law and stockholder restrictions.")
full(38, " The aggregate value of the Settlement Payment under this Agreement is Five Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($537,500.00), comprised of the compensatory damages payment ($275,000.00), the lost wages and incentive compensation payment ($125,000.00), the attorney fees payment ($75,000.00), and the RSU acceleration (valued at $62,500.00 as provided in Section 3(d)). Delano acknowledges that the Settlement Payment exceeds anything of value to which he would otherwise be entitled absent this Agreement, and that no other payment, benefit, or consideration is owed to him or his counsel in connection with the Disputed Claims, including any claim for attorney fees, costs, or interest.", ri=1)
C(P[38], "Arithmetic corrected: $275,000 + $125,000 + $75,000 + $62,500 = $537,500 (draft: $525,000 using outdated $10.00 RSU value).")

# ---------- Section 4 ----------
full(41, "In consideration of the Settlement Payment and other promises set forth in this Agreement, Delano, for himself and on behalf of each of the Releasors, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each of the Releasees from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, extents, executions, losses, expenses, liabilities, and obligations of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, accrued or unaccrued, fixed or contingent, that Delano has, has ever had, or may have against any of the Releasees, arising out of or relating to any act, omission, event, or matter occurring from the beginning of time through the date on which Delano signs this Agreement, including without limitation the Disputed Claims and any claims arising out of, related to, or in any way connected with Delano's employment with Greenleaf, the terms and conditions of that employment, his compensation, benefits, or equity, or the termination thereof.")
C(P[41], "(1) Scope broadened from employment-related claims to all claims, consistent with the title 'General Release of All Claims' and the consideration paid. (2) Cut-off moved from the Effective Date to the date Delano signs: the OWBPA prohibits waiver of ADEA claims arising after execution (29 U.S.C. 626(f)(1)(C)), and a release reaching into the revocation period invites challenge.")
rep(44, [("29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq.;", "29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq., as amended by the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (\"OWBPA\");")])
rep(47, [("29 U.S.C. § 1001 et seq.;", "29 U.S.C. § 1001 et seq. (other than claims for vested benefits);")])
el = after(50, [sub("(viii-a) the whistleblower and employee protection provisions of the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act, 21 U.S.C. § 399d, and Section 11(c) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act, 29 U.S.C. § 660(c);"),
                sub("(viii-b) the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act, 29 U.S.C. § 2101 et seq.;")], ref=SUB)
C(el, "Added the federal whistleblower statutes most directly implicated by Delano's FDA/FSMA cold-chain complaints. A FSMA retaliation claim may still be filed with federal OSHA until approx. Sept. 10, 2025 (180 days from termination). Note: if Delano files a FSMA complaint before signing, settlement of that claim requires OSHA approval (29 C.F.R. 1987.111) - see rep in Section 15(a)(ii).")
rep(51, [("the Oregon Workplace Fairness Act and Oregon's employment discrimination statutes, ORS Chapter 659A;", "the Oregon Workplace Fairness Act and Oregon's employment discrimination statutes, ORS Chapter 659A, including ORS 659A.030, the Oregon Family Leave Act (ORS 659A.150 et seq.), and ORS 659A.040;")])
rep(52, [("including ORS 654.062(5);", "including ORS 654.062(5), ORS 659A.199, and ORS 659A.230 through 659A.233;")])
rep(53, [("including ORS Chapter 652 and ORS Chapter 653;", "including ORS Chapter 652 (including any claim for unpaid wages, bonus, or penalty wages under ORS 652.150) and ORS Chapter 653 (including Oregon sick time, ORS 653.601 et seq.), and the Oregon Equal Pay Act, ORS 652.210 et seq.;")])
full(54, "(xii) claims of discrimination or retaliation relating to workers' compensation, including under ORS 659A.040 (but not claims for workers' compensation benefits under ORS Chapter 656, which are not released by this Agreement);")
C(P[54], "Workers' compensation benefit claims cannot be released by a private settlement in Oregon; a claim disposition agreement requires Workers' Compensation Board approval (ORS 656.236). Purporting to release them risks a court treating the release as overreaching. Retaliation claims under ORS 659A.040 can be released and are now covered.")
el = after(57, [body("Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Released Claims do not include, and nothing in this Agreement waives: (A) Delano's rights under this Agreement; (B) claims for unemployment insurance benefits or workers' compensation benefits; (C) Delano's vested rights under the Greenleaf 401(k) plan or any other ERISA-governed employee benefit plan; (D) Delano's rights under COBRA; (E) claims that arise after the date on which Delano signs this Agreement; (F) Delano's right to challenge the validity of the waiver of ADEA claims under the OWBPA; or (G) any other claim that cannot be waived as a matter of law."),
                (["", ("Section 4A. Protected Rights", True)], None),
                body("Nothing in this Agreement, including Sections 4, 6, 7, 10, and 15, prohibits, prevents, or restricts Delano from: (i) filing a charge or complaint with, communicating with, providing information or documents to, or participating, cooperating, or testifying in any investigation or proceeding conducted by, any Government Agency, including the pending Oregon OSHA investigation relating to Complaint No. OR-OSHA-2024-11872, without notice to or approval from Greenleaf; (ii) testifying truthfully in any legal proceeding or responding to a lawful subpoena or court order; (iii) disclosing or discussing conduct that Delano reasonably believes constitutes unlawful discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or sexual assault, or a violation of food-safety, workplace-safety, or other law, to the extent such disclosure is protected by ORS 659A.370 or other applicable law; (iv) exercising any rights he may have under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act; or (v) making disclosures protected under the Defend Trade Secrets Act, 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) (collectively, \"Protected Rights\"). Delano is not required to withdraw Complaint No. OR-OSHA-2024-11872. However, to the maximum extent permitted by law, Delano waives any right to recover individual monetary relief from any Releasee in any charge, complaint, or lawsuit filed by him or on his behalf asserting any Released Claim, except that nothing in this Agreement limits Delano's right to receive an award from a Government Agency for information provided to that Government Agency.")], ref=BODY)
C(el, "New 'Protected Rights' carve-out (the draft had none). Without it, Sections 4, 6, 7 and 15(a)(ii) (covenant not to file 'any... complaint, charge, or proceeding') would (a) be unenforceable as to EEOC charges and agency participation (EEOC Enforcement Guidance on Non-Waivable Employee Rights; 29 C.F.R. 1625.22(i)); (b) risk violating ORS 659A.370; and (c) most importantly, with the Oregon OSHA investigation of the Bend facility still open, expose Greenleaf to allegations of interfering with a pending agency investigation (ORS 654.062; 18 U.S.C. 1505) and of 'buying silence' on food-safety issues - an independent retaliation theory. The individual-monetary-recovery waiver preserves the economic finality Greenleaf is paying for.")

# ---------- Section 5 ----------
rep(59, [("29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq. Delano further acknowledges and agrees as follows:", "29 U.S.C. §§ 621 et seq. and 626(f). Delano further acknowledges and agrees as follows:")])
full(62, "(c) Delano has been given a period of at least twenty-one (21) calendar days from the date of his receipt of this Agreement on [May __, 2025] within which to consider whether to execute it. Delano may sign this Agreement before the end of that period, but if he does so, he acknowledges that he does so knowingly and voluntarily and not because of any inducement or pressure by Greenleaf, and that Greenleaf has not asked him to shorten that period. The Parties agree that changes to this Agreement, whether material or immaterial, made after Delano first received this revised Agreement do not restart the twenty-one (21) day consideration period.")

Both deliverables are in /workspace/output. The markup redlines the Engel & Associates draft for Greenleaf with tracked changes and 33 margin comments; the main fixes are an ADEA release that complies with the federal waiver rules, the corrected equity value, and removal of the non-compete. The memo to the GC sets out the issues, risks, business decisions and steps needed before signing. Both files pass the docx validation check and open cleanly when read back.

- **ADEA release:** Delano is 58, and the draft would not have validly released his age claim. It now gives him 21 days to consider and 7 days to revoke, and the Effective Date is tied to his signature.
- **Equity value:** the draft priced the RSUs at $10.00/share, an outdated valuation. The current one is $12.50 (January 15, 2025), so the RSUs are worth $62,500 and the total is $537,500, not $525,000. The acceleration also needs Compensation Committee approval because the shares were forfeited at termination.
- **Non-compete:** deleted as void under Oregon's non-compete statute (ORS 653.295). It is replaced by a new confidentiality and trade-secret section, and the non-solicit is kept.
- **Protected rights:** added a clause preserving Delano's right to deal with government agencies, since the Oregon OSHA investigation is still open.
- **Tax:** attorney fees moved from Form 1099-NEC to 1099-MISC. The back-pay description now covers the undetermined 2024 bonus. Delano now indemnifies Greenleaf for taxes on the non-wage payments.

The memo also flags open items to confirm, including:
- EPLI carrier consent to the settlement.
- Whether anyone else was let go in the restructuring (if so, the review period becomes 45 days).
- Whether the COO, Patricia Engel, is related to Delano's counsel, Rachel Engel.
- Whether Delano actually asked for the confidentiality terms.
- The replacement hired six days after the termination.

I dated the memo and tracked changes May 12, 2025, to fit the record (the HR summary is dated May 10, 2025).
